clips.scene: A single, clean line of European soldiers standing shoulder to shoulder on a churned, overcast battlefield near Legnica, Poland, April 9, 1241 — ONE line only, not multiple messy clusters. HAZEL is walking INSIDE this line, IN THE GAPS BETWEEN the soldiers (in among the ranks, part of the formation's own depth), NOT behind it and NOT outside looking at it from a distance. Because she is standing among them facing the SAME direction they are (the open horizon where the threat will come from), the soldiers immediately beside her are seen in SIDE PROFILE, each actively gripping a kite shield in their forward arm held OUT IN FRONT of their body facing outward toward the horizon (a shield is never slung or worn on the back while standing in line — it is always held actively facing the direction of the threat), spear in the other hand, point leveled forward. Everyone in the line — her included — faces the same direction. Every visible soldier does constant, disciplined micro-movement: adjusting a shield grip, resetting a spear, shifting weight, checking a neighbor's gear, bracing — never idle, never aimless wandering. She is urgent, delivering her FULL line uninterrupted. The INSTANT she finishes speaking, a war horn suddenly sounds — she turns sharply toward the same direction the whole line is already facing, the view swinging past her own shoulder toward the horizon; the shot ENDS on her alarmed profile as she registers that something is there, before anything on the horizon is clearly visible yet (the reveal itself is the NEXT clip, not this one).
clips.dialogue: HAZEL (breathless, urgent, to lens, COMPLETE sentence, not cut off): "April, 1241. Europe is about to face the Mongols."
clips.action: Single continuous unbroken shot, one camera angle throughout, no cuts, no scene changes, real-time continuous take. She is walking the entire time, moving along INSIDE the single line of soldiers (among them, in the gaps between files), never behind the line looking at backs, never outside/distant from it. Soldiers beside her are seen in profile with their shields clearly held forward/outward, never on their backs. She delivers her full line clearly and completely — do NOT cut off or interrupt her dialogue. The horn sounds right as she finishes the line (interrupting the moment/beat afterward, not her speech), and she turns sharply in reaction to it, in the SAME direction the whole line is already facing (not an arbitrary direction, not toward the soldiers' backs). End the shot on her alarmed/startled expression looking toward the horizon, NOT on a resolved view of the Mongol army — that reveal belongs to the next clip.
clips.sound: Wind, banners snapping, the creak/clink of soldiers adjusting gear and shifting stance, horses breathing nearby, distant murmur of the forming line, then a SUDDEN loud war horn right as she finishes speaking

clips.scene: HAZEL is still facing the horizon, facing the lens. Her arm/hand position for the selfie framing is CONSTANT from the first frame to the last — it never drops to her side and re-raises partway through; if she needs a free hand to react or tremble, she uses the OTHER hand only. From the VERY FIRST FRAME of this shot to the last, it contains ONLY her and the Mongol force — ZERO European soldiers, mounted or on foot, ZERO shields/crosses/banners belonging to the European side, at ANY point including the opening moment. Do not carry over any element of the previous scene's European formation into this shot's composition, even briefly. The terrain is open, empty battlefield ground — bare mud/dirt, dust — with NO tents, NO camp structures. NO slow layered build — the full chaotic scale is visible essentially immediately: a vast, dust-churning mass of Mongol cavalry already in motion, individual riders and horses distinct within the chaos. Mongol banners and shields use plain, geometric, or tribal/totemic steppe patterning appropriate to a Tengrist/shamanist culture — ABSOLUTELY NO crosses, NO European-style heraldry. A COMMANDER splits off from the main mass and rides directly up to her, REINING HIS HORSE TO A FULL STOP facing her — a genuine pause in the chaos for a real exchange, not a passing glance. He is dressed unmistakably as Mongol, NOT European: lamellar/leather armor (no mail hauberk, no plate), a distinctive fur-trimmed or leather steppe helmet (explicitly NOT a European conical/segmented helmet), a curved sabre at his belt. His helmet/framing is open-faced so his face is clearly visible and readable the entire time. He faces her directly and stays facing her for the whole exchange — he does NOT turn away or ride off mid-line. She is visibly frightened — trembling, voice unsteady — NOT shouting, NOT confrontational, but manages to speak despite her fear. Only after he finishes his line does he turn his horse and ride back to rejoin the charge.
clips.dialogue: HAZEL (frightened, voice shaking, quiet with effort — NOT yelling or confrontational; she is a neutral time-traveler, not bound to either side, so addressing the commander directly is in character even while scared): "Grandsons of Genghis Khan..." [he reins his horse to a full stop, faces her directly, face clearly visible] "You already burned Beijing to the ground. Why are you here?" [MONGOL COMMANDER, facing her the entire time, calm and imperious, does NOT turn away or ride off while speaking — dialogue is cinematic reconstruction, not a documented quotation, same disclosure as Henry's lines]: "The world is not so easily finished." [beat — only now does he turn his horse and ride back toward the charge; she watches, then turns her body toward camp/Henry's position as the shot ends — bridges into clip 2]
clips.action: Single continuous unbroken shot, one camera angle throughout, no cuts, no scene changes, real-time continuous take. Her selfie-framing arm position is constant throughout — no dropping and re-raising. The full scale of the charging horde is visible from very early in the shot. No European soldiers, foot or mounted, ever appear in this shot, including the opening frame. This is a genuine STOPPED, FACE-TO-FACE conversation, not a passing shout — the commander reins to a full stop and faces her for the whole exchange, never turning away mid-line. His armor/helmet must read unmistakably Mongol (lamellar, steppe helmet), never European plate/conical helmet. Her emotional register is frightened and trembling, not aggressive or shouting. The main charge/attack itself does NOT reach her in this clip — that arrives in the next clip. By the end of the shot she is turning her body away from the horizon toward camp. Do not render the cavalry as a flat, repeated, or synthetic-looking silhouette.
clips.sound: The war horn's echo fading, then a rising rumble of thousands of hooves, distant Mongol horns answering, wind carrying dust

clips.scene: Opens continuing the exact turning motion clip 1B ended on (motion continuation, not a fresh static start) — HAZEL arrives at Duke Henry II the Pious, mounted on his horse, facing the lens with Henry visible over her shoulder/beside her in the same frame (never a separate reverse shot of him alone). Her wardrobe remains her established madder-red kirtle, undyed linen apron, and kerchief throughout this entire shot, unchanged and unsubstituted. Henry is at the head of a VAST host of his own men, ALL FACING THE SAME OPEN-FIELD DIRECTION HENRY FACES — toward where the enemy stands — not a small cluster, not a few dozen, but a massive coalition force filling the visible ground close around him and extending back in depth rank after rank until it fades into the haze near the horizon: mounted knights nearest him, dense ranks of spearmen and shield-bearers behind, countless banners planted throughout. Every soldier's face, body, and shield face that SAME enemy-facing direction as Henry — NEVER shown from behind with their backs to the camera or to the enemy side. Every shield-bearer holds his kite shield ACTIVELY OUT IN FRONT of his body facing outward toward the enemy direction — a shield is NEVER slung or visible on a soldier's back. Individually distinct riders/soldiers throughout (varied poses, visible individual gear), never a flat/repeated/synthetic-looking mass. The men immediately around Henry are a loose, unformed crowd at the start (standing, shifting, adjusting gear, not yet organized into ranks), but even unformed they face the enemy direction, never with backs turned to it. For the FINAL beat of this same continuous shot: HAZEL, STILL FULLY VISIBLE IN FRAME THE ENTIRE TIME (never dropping out of shot, not even briefly), turns her body and the camera together (one single unbroken shot, a whip-turn, not a cut) to face the OPPOSITE side of the open field from Henry's host — the two armies positioned on directly opposite sides of the same open battlefield, FACING EACH OTHER across the ground, never side-by-side and never the same depth-of-field as Henry's men. On that far, opposite side: a vast MONGOL CAVALRY host — matching the identity already established in clip 1B, NOT generic foot infantry — mounted riders on horseback (not on foot), dressed unmistakably as Mongol: lamellar/leather armor (no mail hauberk, no plate), distinctive fur-trimmed or leather steppe helmets (NOT European conical/segmented helmets), curved sabres, composite bows visible on many riders, banners and any shields using plain/geometric/tribal steppe patterning (ABSOLUTELY NO crosses, NO European heraldry). Matching Henry's side in scale and individual distinctness (not a flat/synthetic mass), every rider FACING TOWARD Henry's side (never shown from behind, never riding or facing away), ADVANCING AT A SLOW, DELIBERATE WALKING PACE on horseback toward Henry's line — NOT galloping, NOT charging, NOT at speed — a slow, ominous advance, with the actual charge saved for clip 3.
clips.dialogue: HAZEL (arriving, still completing the turn/approach from 1B): "Duke Henry the Second. He's leading them." HAZEL (to Henry, still facing the lens): "How many are we fighting?" [Henry] (grim, eyes on the horizon, visible in her frame): "Enough." [beat — Henry keeps watching the horizon and is the one who spots the approaching Mongols himself — no gesture or prompt from her] [Henry, shouting]: "Hold the line!" [the INSTANT he shouts this, his own nearby men visibly react — turning, moving, closing ranks, organizing from their loose crowd into a proper line formation around him, all facing the enemy direction, shields forward] [she turns her whole body — still fully in frame throughout, camera turning with her in the same unbroken shot — to see what he's reacting to, revealing the Mongol cavalry host on the opposite side of the field, facing toward Henry's side, advancing slowly on horseback, not charging; the shot ends on this reveal, bridging directly into clip 3]
clips.action: Henry looks to the horizon BEFORE he answers "Enough" — the look precedes the line. He keeps watching the horizon after answering her, and he is the one who spots the approaching Mongols himself; that sighting is what makes him shout "Hold the line!" — no pointing or prompting from her, that gesture stays cut entirely. His stance keeps him oriented toward the enemy-facing direction throughout, turning only his head/shoulders toward Hazel when directly speaking to her, never presenting his back to the enemy side. The instant he shouts, his own nearby soldiers (an unformed loose crowd until now) visibly react — turning, moving, closing ranks into a proper line formation around him, ALL FACING the same enemy direction Henry faces, shields held actively forward toward that direction, NEVER on their backs, NEVER shown from behind. Immediately after, she turns her entire body to see what he reacted to, the camera turning with her in the SAME continuous unbroken shot (a whip-turn, not a cut, no scene change) — CRITICAL: she must remain fully visible in frame for the ENTIRE turn, at no point dropping out of shot even briefly. Her wardrobe (madder-red kirtle, apron, kerchief) stays visually consistent and unchanged throughout this turn. The turn reveals the OPPOSITE side of the open field from Henry's host — the Mongol CAVALRY force (mounted riders on horseback, matching clip 1B's established lamellar-armor/steppe-helmet identity, NOT foot infantry) is positioned across from Henry's line, the two armies FACING EACH OTHER over open ground, neither side ever shown from behind or riding/facing away. The revealed Mongol host matches Henry's side in scale (a vast, individually-distinct force, not a flat/synthetic mass), every rider facing toward Henry's side, advancing at a slow, deliberate WALK on horseback, not a gallop or charge — building dread through pace, not speed. End the shot on this reveal and her alarmed reaction, ready to bridge directly into clip 3's charge.
clips.sound: Wind, restless horses, low murmur of nobles, Henry's voice grim and commanding, then the low rumble of many marching hooves and feet at a walking pace becoming audible as she turns to face them

clips.scene: Continuing directly from clip 2's ending position — HAZEL has just completed her whip-turn to face the Mongol cavalry host on the far side of the open field. Their slow, deliberate walking advance from clip 2 closes into a full gallop charge in the very first moment of this shot — the same motion continuing, not a fresh unrelated start. She is crouched low, facing the oncoming Mongol cavalry — her flinching, frightened reaction and the charging horse archers are visible together in the same continuous selfie framing, facing the lens. The Mongol riders match the identity already established in clips 1B and 2: mounted on horseback, lamellar/leather armor (no mail hauberk, no plate), fur-trimmed steppe helmets (NOT European conical/segmented helmets), composite bows drawn and firing as they close distance — NOT foot infantry, NOT European gear. European soldiers from Henry's line FLANK HER ON BOTH HER LEFT AND HER RIGHT (visible on both sides in the same frame), facing that SAME oncoming direction she faces (never shown from behind, never facing away) — they are ACTIVELY ENGAGED, not idle or standing still: bracing their stance, shouting to each other, raising their kite shields OUT IN FRONT of their bodies, held forward toward the incoming charge, never on their backs. Arrows THUD into those raised, forward-facing shields on both her left and right in the same continuous motion as the charge escalates — embedded within the shot, not a separate beat. As the charge reaches its closest point, the Mongol riders visibly wheel and peel away in multiple directions, breaking off — a real, confusing reversal she reacts to directly, still in the same continuous shot.
clips.dialogue: HAZEL (short, breathless, AT the moment the charge closes distance — not before): "They're moving—" [arrows begin thudding into the raised shields flanking her on both sides] [beat — the Mongol riders visibly wheel and peel away, breaking off the charge] HAZEL (confused, still breathless, watching them go): "Wait— they're retreating?" [beat — she catches herself] HAZEL (urgent, to lens): "No. Watch. This is what they do — they lure you into chasing them, then they turn back and finish you."
clips.action: Single continuous unbroken shot, one camera angle throughout, no cuts, no scene changes, real-time continuous take. The charge closes from the slow walk established at the end of clip 2 to a full gallop in the opening instant of this shot — not a fresh, unrelated start. She stays crouched, facing the charge the entire time, her flinching reaction and the oncoming riders sharing the same frame throughout. European soldiers flank her visibly on BOTH her left and right sides, facing the same oncoming direction as her, ACTIVELY bracing, shouting, and raising their kite shields out in front, held forward toward the charge — never idle, never standing passively, never shields on their backs, never facing away — and arrows visibly thud into those forward-facing shields on both sides as the charge closes. Only once the charge is at its closest does it break off — the Mongol riders visibly wheeling/peeling away in different directions — and her dialogue about the retreat comes AFTER she can actually see them turning away, not before (dialogue-action causality). She delivers her explanation line while the riders are still visible retreating in the background of the same shot.
clips.sound: The rumble of hooves breaking into a full thundering gallop, war cries, the whistle and thud of arrows striking raised shields on both sides, her own ragged breathing, then the hoofbeats receding as the riders wheel away

clips.scene: Direct visual continuation of clip 3's peel-away — the SAME retreating Mongol cavalry she just watched wheel and turn are the ones now receding ahead in the distance, not new or different riders. She straightens slightly from her crouch, still facing the lens, tracking those same retreating riders as MULTIPLE European soldiers/knights (a populated pursuit, several visible, not just one man) surge past close beside her in the same frame, already at a run/gallop, chasing after the retreating Mongols. The nearest soldier is already beside her in frame before he speaks — not appearing out of nowhere — his face open and clearly visible as he shouts, celebratory and completely unaware this is a trap.
clips.dialogue: SOLDIER (in her frame, mid-stride, surging past close beside her, celebratory, unaware of the trap): "They're fleeing! After them!" HAZEL (horrified, NOT celebrating — she alone understands what this means after what she just explained in the previous moment): "No— don't chase them!" [her warning lost in the noise and momentum of the pursuit already sweeping past her]
clips.action: Single continuous unbroken shot, no cuts, no scene changes, real-time continuous take. She straightens from her crouch but stays urgent, tracking the SAME retreating riders from clip 3 as they recede — not a fresh, unrelated group. Multiple European soldiers/knights surge past close beside her in the same frame, already at a run, chasing the retreating Mongols — a populated pursuit, not a single soldier standing in for the whole event. The nearest soldier is already beside her in frame before his line — not a fresh appearance — his face visible and readable as he shouts. His celebratory line comes first (dialogue-action causality: he's reacting to the retreat he can see), and her horrified warning comes immediately after, as a direct reaction to the pursuit sweeping past her, not before it. End the shot with the pursuit still surging past/around her, unresolved, ready to sweep her into clip 5.
clips.sound: The receding hoofbeats of the retreating Mongols mixing with the surging hoofbeats and footfalls of the pursuing Europeans, shouts and cheers of the pursuit, her own voice nearly lost in the noise

clips.scene: Opens already IN the pursuit that ended clip 4 — motion continuation, not a fresh start; SHE HERSELF RUNS FORWARD, moving in the exact same direction and matching the same running pace as the soldiers surging past her — never static, never rigidly face-on while everyone around her is in forward motion; the selfie framing holds steady on her because the camera moves forward with her at the same speed, not because she is standing still or drifting backward relative to the crowd. Ahead of her, in the same lane/direction the pursuing European riders are already committed to, the Mongol cavalry (same identity established in clips 1B/2/3: mounted, lamellar/leather armor, fur-trimmed steppe helmets, composite bows) visibly WHEEL AROUND to face the pursuit head-on — a real, sudden reversal directly in the pursuers' path, not an unrelated new group off to the side. Simultaneously, additional Mongol cavalry becomes visible entering from a flank at the frame's edge, already in motion — the pursuit is being enveloped from more than one direction. Arrows begin arcing down out of the sky around her and the nearby soldiers as the trap closes — non-graphic: only the visible arc and the thud of arrows landing in mud or striking nearby soldiers' shields — those shields still held forward, facing outward, never on their backs — no depicted impact on any person. She brings her framing in tighter on her own face as she reacts, her selfie-framing arm position staying constant throughout.
clips.dialogue: HAZEL (grim, NOT surprised — dread, watching it happen exactly as she already warned): "They pulled them straight out of formation. Just like I told them—" [arrows begin arcing down around her, physically cutting off the rest of her line as she dives for cover]
clips.action: Single continuous unbroken shot, one camera angle throughout, no cuts, no scene changes, real-time continuous take, opening already in motion from clip 4's pursuit — not a fresh start. She runs forward the entire time, matching the same pace and direction as the pursuit around her — her body leans into the run, legs and arms in genuine running motion, never a static or rigid pose that would read as her moving backward relative to the soldiers surging past her. The Mongol riders ahead of her wheel around to face the pursuit directly, in the same lane the pursuing Europeans are already committed to. Additional Mongol cavalry becomes visible entering from a flank at the frame's edge, in motion, as the envelopment begins. Arrows arc down and land around her and nearby soldiers — visible motion and impact into ground or into soldiers' shields (held forward, facing outward, never on their backs) only, no graphic injury depicted on any person. Her line is cut off mid-sentence by the arrows starting to fall, not spoken calmly to completion (dialogue-action causality: the danger interrupts her mid-thought). She then dives for cover as the shot ends, her selfie-framing arm position staying constant throughout the dive. End the shot on the completion of that dive, ready for clip 6 to open on the same position, not a new pose.
clips.sound: The chaos of the pursuit abruptly changing pitch — hooves wheeling and reversing direction, new war cries from the flanking cavalry, the whistle and thud of arrows raining down, shouts of alarm from the European soldiers around her
